item.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption compares corruption risk management in local councils and state agencies to support benchmarking.
item.support: This report compares the corruption risk management of local councils and state agencies within NSW.

item.text: It analyses survey responses from public sector organisations and staff, gathered in 2007.
item.support: During 2007, as part of the Profiling the NSW public sector II project

item.text: The Commission concludes that councils face a broader range of risks from their functions and processes, while fewer appear to use management controls than state agencies.
item.support: The clearest finding is that fewer local councils appear to adopt management controls than state agencies.

item.text: The Commission advises councils to review management controls and computer-password practices, and cautions that survey comparisons cannot replace assessment of each organisation’s risks.
item.support: this process cannot give a complete picture of an organisation’s corruption prevention strengths and vulnerabilities.

item.quote: The clearest finding is that fewer local councils appear to adopt management controls than state agencies.
Corruption risks arising from staff misconduct do not appear to differ greatly between local councils and state agencies in NSW.
